intro.text: A hospital wants a new appointment system. Before anyone writes code, two questions must be answered.

what.text: First: what should the system do? That is analysis. Collect the facts, find the problems, and break the system into its parts.

how.text: Second: how will the system do it? That is design. Plan the modules, the screens, the databases, and the interfaces.

order.text: Analysis specifies what. Design focuses on how. Always in that order.

fourp.text: Every project has four P's. People: the stakeholders. Product: the software, plus its documents. Project: the activities. And process: the framework that orders those activities.

success.text: A project succeeds when the system meets the user needs, is delivered on time, and stays within budget.

defect.text: Quality means meeting the requirements. A defect is a deviation from the requirements.

cost.text: And the earlier a defect is found, the less it costs to repair.

verif.text: Two checks protect quality. Verification asks: are we building the product right? Does the code follow the design? Inspections and reviews are verification.

valid.text: Validation asks: are we building the right product? Does the system meet the user requirements? Testing is validation.
